root_motivation: Who: an agent with no file tool following the llms.txt database-in-a-minute recipe, and the live judge that proves it. What: host_table_create imports a CSV from a source_url, but the fixture URL the predecessor's live AC named, https://mcphost.dev/examples/sample-1000.csv, is served by nothing and answers 404 on prod, and the live verifier had no tenant credential. Why they cannot: the file sits in the repo but no route serves it, no drift test ties an advertised example URL to a route, and no committed driver mints its own synthetic tenant. Cost: the discovery chain's truth-recipe-mcphost-database-in-a-minute link completes at 0.00 because the recipe offers only five batched appends.
user_persona: An agent that creates the 1,000-row table with one host_table_create call from a public URL; Operator Joe, who reads one results line from a committed driver instead of a transcript.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the binary's static routes, When `GET /examples/sample-1000.csv` is requested, Then it answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, the same `Cache-Control` as `/llms.txt`, and a body byte-identical to `examples/database-in-a-minute/fixture.csv` (header plus 1,000 data rows).

Given every absolute example-fixture URL (`/examples/<file>` on the public origin) found under `agent/`, `recipes/`, `www/`, `docs/` and `examples/`, When the route drift test runs, Then each path is a route in the binary's static-route table, and the test fails on a URL that has none.

Given `scripts/live/tblurlp_import_live.py` and the loopback harness app serving its own fixture route, When the driver runs with `--base-url http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, Then its last line starts with `fixture_http=200 rows_imported=1000 count=1000 is_error=0` and it exits 0, and `--plan` prints the steps with no network call.

Given prod `/mcp`, When the committed driver signs up a synthetic tenant, creates `tblurlp_ac04` from `source_url` `https://mcphost.dev/examples/sample-1000.csv`, counts it and offboards, Then the row passes (Live; evidence: `~/.local/state/mcphost-live/tblurlp-ac04-results.jsonl` last row `summary` `fixture_http=200 rows_imported=1000 count=1000 is_error=0 offboarded=1`)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred: Live (prod; evidence: ~/.local/state/mcphost-live/tblurlp-ac04-results.jsonl last row summary; operator-provisioned)

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the hand-written `## Give Claude a database in one minute` section of `www/llms.txt`, When an agent reads it, Then the one-call form (`host_table_create` with `source_url` `https://mcphost.dev/examples/sample-1000.csv`) comes before the batched-append step, and the AC 2 drift test covers that URL.

scope: src/http.rs: static route GET /examples/sample-1000.csv serving examples/database-in-a-minute/fixture.csv as text/csv.
scripts/live/tblurlp_import_live.py: the stdlib driver (synthetic signup, host_table_create from source_url, host_table_count, host_self_offboard) and its proof lane.
www/llms.txt: the hand-written database-in-a-minute section leads with the one-call source_url form.
non_goals: Any new file under www/ or mcphost-deploy change; any fetch-guard change; the generated recipe:database-in-a-minute block; the synthorg chain's recipe prompt.

additional.live_driver: stdlib python only; the minted key lives in a 0600 file under mktemp -d, shredded on exit, never printed.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did live AC 7 of the predecessor fail?
five_whys_trace.a: It fetched a fixture URL that prod answers with 404.
No AC published the file and the binary served no route for it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why could the live verifier not create a tenant?
five_whys_trace.a: No committed driver signs up its own synthetic tenant; the admin key is refused by host_table_create.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which Cache-Control does the fixture route carry?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The same as /llms.txt, which sets none; the test compares the two headers.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Is agent/intent-card.json AC text scanned by the drift test?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Yes, agents read the card, so an advertised URL there needs a route like any other.
